This is a draft placeholder, not a tested setup guide or a review of the apps mentioned
below. It sketches the questions a future article could investigate.

## One task list, many devices

The idea sounds simple: keep tasks on mailbox.org and use whichever app feels at home on
each device. CalDAV provides the connection, and iCalendar's `VTODO` component
represents the tasks. In practice, agreeing on a protocol does not mean that every app
supports the same features or presents them in the same way.

A task created on an iPad should still make sense on an Android phone, a Linux laptop, a
Windows PC, and an iPhone. The interesting question is not just whether it appears, but
whether its due date, notes, recurrence, reminders, and completion status survive a
round trip through different apps.

## A different app for every platform

- **iOS and iPadOS:** Apple Reminders can connect to CalDAV accounts, although Apple
  notes that some features are unavailable outside iCloud. Which task properties work
  with mailbox.org would need to be checked on both devices.
- **Android:** DAVx⁵ can synchronize CalDAV collections with compatible task apps such
  as Tasks.org or jtx Board. The sync adapter and the app each have a part to play in
  what can be stored and edited.
- **Linux and Windows:** KOrganizer is one possible client on both systems; mailbox.org
  documents connecting its calendars and tasks through CalDAV. Other clients and their
  task support deserve a closer look as well.
- **In the browser:** The mailbox.org interface provides another view of the data and a
  useful reference when checking what actually reached the server.

## Where compatibility becomes complicated

Seeing the same title on every device is only the beginning. Some clients may not expose
all properties, while others may interpret or update them differently. Recurring tasks,
subtasks, priorities, reminders, time zones, and completed items are especially useful
things to examine. A feature missing from an app is different from a broken standard:
the result can still be frustrating when an edit in one place changes what another app
shows.

Synchronization adds its own questions. How quickly do changes arrive? What happens when
two devices edit the same task offline? Does an app preserve fields it cannot show? And
if a task disappears, was it filtered locally, moved to another list, or changed on the
server?

## A useful test before committing

A future version of this post could follow a small set of tasks through every client:
create one with a due date and notes, add a recurring task and a subtask, then edit and
complete them on different devices. Checking the mailbox.org interface between steps
would help distinguish a sync problem from a display problem. The outcome should be a
record of what was tested, including app versions and limitations, rather than an
assumption that every CalDAV implementation behaves alike.

For setup details and background, see the [mailbox.org KOrganizer
guide](https://kb.mailbox.org/en/private/addressbook-and-calendar/caldav-korganizer/),
[Apple's Reminders account
guide](https://support.apple.com/en-ie/guide/iphone/iph8739025dd/ios), and the [DAVx⁵
task app overview](https://www.davx5.com/faq/tasks/advanced-task-features).
